title: AI Research Engineer (New York)

ABOUT EDRA

Edra is solving one of the hardest problems in enterprise AI: AI models are generic but company processes are specific. We build AI agents that learn how processes actually run, and then run their operations.

We're a Series A startup, backed by Sequoia and other leading VC firms, led by Co-Founders who created and led Forward Deployed AI Engineering at Palantir, and we're growing our team in New York and London. We're a deeply technical team of engineers, AI researchers, and strategists with a high bar for talent and a shared belief that exceptional people are the foundation of everything great we'll build.

THE ROLE

We're building a learning system that teaches AI agents how enterprises actually work. Our system starts from what a customer already has: knowledge base articles, support conversations, tickets, system logs, and agent traces. From that evidence it reverse-engineers how the business actually runs and writes the process down as instructions a person can inspect and an agent can execute, with confidence scoring to know when to automate and when to seek human input.

We're looking for AI Research Engineers who have built complex, production LLM-based systems. Whether you've scaled LLM workflows handling millions of requests, built multi-agent systems in production, or designed evaluation frameworks for enterprise deployments, we want people who bring intensity and self-direction to their craft. You'll work on our agentic learning environment: the loops that turn human corrections and agent outcomes into better knowledge and instructions over time. The job combines applied research with ownership of production systems. You find a failure, form a hypothesis, run the experiment, and ship the fix into real customer workflows.

You'll spend most of your time advancing our core context-learning library and the harness that powers our agents across every customer. The work spans continuous learning, context engineering, agent orchestration, and evaluation. You'll contribute to our knowledge benchmarks and to the self-improving capabilities of the harness.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Build and extend our core context-learning library, turning customer-informed problems into reusable platform capabilities.

- Design and implement LLM-powered systems and agentic workflows from concept to production.

- Build agentic features for knowledge management: agents that can edit, update, and maintain large knowledge bases autonomously.

- Build continuous learning loops that use human corrections and production outcomes to find knowledge gaps, detect changed procedures, and improve prompts and instructions.

- Build reliability and confidence systems: evaluation frameworks, confidence scoring, and logic for when to automate and when to escalate to a human.

- Architect async, scalable systems that handle complex AI orchestration.

- Contribute to the direction of our AI strategy and product capabilities.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

- You've built a complex, production LLM system with real depth: multiple layers of engineering decisions you can walk through, including what changed after real users arrived.

- You have practical depth in one or more of context engineering, retrieval, agent orchestration, memory, evaluation, or learning from feedback.

- You have experimental judgment. You can turn an ambiguous problem into a testable hypothesis, set a baseline, and tell a real improvement from noise.

- You're excited by open-ended problems where the solution might not exist yet.

This is a senior leadership role on the Partnerships leadership team, reporting to the Global Head of Partnerships.

A deployment starts with work the business wants an agent to do: a research process in a bank, claims handling at an insurer, engineering workflows in a retailer. A partner's engineers build it against the customer's own systems and data, evaluate it on real work rather than a demo, and put it live. What you will own

• Deployment strategy and approached. Bringing the best ways to deploy Claude to our customers through partners: which deployment approaches we back, which partners we build them with, and how both change as the models and the use cases move.

Our own people, in region, alongside the partner's team on live engagements: they run the delivery cadence, hold the work to date and quality, and are the first to know when something is going wrong. Where a partner's own delivery practice meets that standard, you approve them to carry the work and you assure the result.

title: Document Controller & Administrator

Document Controller & Administrator - Nordics
Location :Remote, based anywhere in Sweden, Finland, Norway, or Denmark, with occasional in person meetings in Stockholm and travel to Nordic project sites.
Schedule : Full time.
Who are we?
At Vertiv , we're on a mission to power the people and technologies that keep the world connected. From data centres to telecom networks and industrial facilities, our solutions ensure that critical systems stay online no matter what.
With over $10.2 billion in revenue and operations spanning nearly 70 countries, Vertiv offers the stability of a global leader and the excitement of a fast evolving industry.
About the Role
Vertiv is hiring a Document Controller & Administrator to join our growing Nordics team. This is a key support role within our project delivery function, ensuring that all documentation across our Nordic projects is accurately managed, controlled, and accessible to the right people at the right time.
What You'll Be Doing
You will be responsible for managing the full document control lifecycle across our Nordic projects, working within systems such as Asite, SharePoint, Procore, ACC, and Dalux. This means ensuring all drawings, specifications, and technical documents are logged, version controlled, and distributed correctly with the appropriate revision status and transmittals. You will track and manage RFIs, submittals, material approvals, technical queries, and responses, making sure superseded documents are removed from circulation and properly archived.
Beyond document control, you will provide day to day administrative support to the Project Manager and Site Teams. This includes managing site correspondence such as emails, letters, and reports, maintaining filing systems, and coordinating meetings by scheduling site and client meetings, recording minutes, and distributing action trackers. You will also maintain key site registers including drawing registers, document logs, and site diaries, as well as managing site deliveries and spare parts ordering systems.
The role includes some travel around the Nordics to support our Project and Site Managers in the deployment of projects. You will work with internal and external partners throughout the full project lifecycle, from implementation through to final closure.
What We're Looking For

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Strong organisational and time management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities.
- Experience with document control systems (e.g. Asite, SharePoint, Procore, ACC, Dalux) is a strong advantage.
- Fully proficient in Microsoft Office and other document management software.
- Self motivated and capable of working with minimal supervision.
- A flexible, multi tasking approach to work.

- Excellent customer service skills.
- A valid full driving licence.

• Fluent English language skills (Nordic languages are an advantage).

Who You'll Work With
Internally, you will work closely with Sales, Service, Project Management, Factories, and Suppliers. Externally, you will be the point of contact for Clients, Consultants, Contractors, and End Users, ensuring communication is clear, professional, and in line with the Vertiv business culture.
What's In It For You

• The opportunity to join a global leader in critical infrastructure at an exciting time of growth in the Nordics.
- A predominantly remote role with flexibility to be based anywhere in Sweden, Finland, Norway, or Denmark.
- Full training and support from a global network of technical experts.
- Modern tools and systems to help you succeed.
- Career development and progression opportunities within a high performance culture.
- The chance to be part of building something new as Vertiv expands its Nordic operation.

The successful candidate will embrace Vertiv 's Core Principles & Behaviours to help execute our Strategic Priorities.
